newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hanwa's successor bank to have 10 bln yen capital.
newsitem.headline: Hanwa's successor bank to have 10 bln yen capital.

text.p: A new bank to take over the operations of the now defunct Hanwa Bank Ltd will be capitalised at 10 billion yen, the Finance Ministry announced on Friday.
Last month, the ministry ordered the second-tier regional bank, which had been suffering under the weight of problem loans, to halt its operations.

A senior ministry official said the new bank will only be responsible for handling deposit withdrawals and will shut down after taking care of Hanwa's remaining business. Asked if the new bank will be responsible for dealing with failures of any banks in the future, the official said: "At the moment, we do not have such a plan."
He said the new bank is expected to be established by the end of the current fiscal year in March 31, 1997.
The official said the capital for the new bank will come from a special fund set up by the government earlier this year to handle failures of Japan's housing loan companies.

To be precise, the 10 billion yen will come from the 100 billion yen put up by the Bank of Japan for the special fund, the official said. "Since it's funded by the Bank of Japan, the new bank cannot exist forever," he said.
The official said Hanwa's assets will be purchased by the Deposit Insurance Corp, which will ask the Resolution and Collection Bank to collect the bank's outstanding loans.
A senior Bank of Japan official told a separate news conference that the central bank had decided to support the plan because no private banks showed interest in providing funds to the new bank.
"The amount of the capital was not that small, partly because if the amount is too small, depositors would become worried," the BOJ official said.
